rows.caution: READ IT WITH `tax_collection`, WHICH IS THE SAME TABLE FOR OTHER YEARS -- UNION them, never join. Column names differ between the two (`balance_forward` here, `forward` there). The printed COLUMN ORDER changes mid-archive, and FY2023 and FY2024 are both headed `FY2021 COLLECTION OF TAXES`, so the fiscal year cannot be read off the heading. Years absent here are in `receivables_reconciliation` with a reason.

rows.grain: one row per levy or charge, per year
rows.what_it_answers: The same RECEIVABLES SUMMARY, for FY2014, FY2015 and FY2025 -- the years that carry a real PDF text layer rather than a scan, and so read exact to the cent.
rows.caution: ONE TABLE, TWO READERS, PARTITIONED BY YEAR WITH NO OVERLAP. It skips at runtime every year `receivables` proves. UNION the two for the full series (9 of 15 years tie to the Collector's own printed GRAND TOTAL); never join them. Refusals and their reasons are in `tax_collection_unreconciled`.

rows.grain: one row per class, per table, per edition
rows.what_it_answers: What the town is worth and the levy on it: valuation and levy by major class, new growth, average values, the LA4 totals and the levy build-up, FY2011-FY2025.
rows.caution: SPLIT ON `status`. FY2021 is `check failed` because its page REPRINTS FY2020’s TOTALS row -- its four class rows sum $194,412,308 above the total printed beneath them. Prefer this over `report_valuation`, which covers the same pages and whose every row is `no check`: one column ruler cannot serve the three or four tables the Assessors print on one page.

rows.grain: one row per project, per plan year
rows.what_it_answers: The Capital Planning Committee's ranked recommendation, FY2015-FY2023 -- which extends `capital_plan_fy27` backwards nine years.
rows.caution: WHAT WAS ASKED FOR, NOT WHAT WAS FUNDED. FY2016 prints both and this holds the Committee's list; `capital_funding_history` holds the funded figure. A different table from `report_capital_projects`, which is the fund balance schedule.

rows.grain: one row per line item or ledger line, per year
rows.what_it_answers: The cable access fund, FY2015-FY2025: what Comcast pays the town under the licence, and what it buys -- salaries, equipment, expenses.
rows.caution: IT IS IN NO BUDGET LINE ANYBODY VOTES ON, which is the point of it: this money pays real staff and appears in no appropriation, so a reader of the budget alone cannot see the people it employs (rule 11). Three years disagree with themselves and are recorded rather than reconciled -- FY2017's printed TOTAL omits a $450.00 vendor expense, and FY2025's ending balance ignores the year's own $262,565 of revenue.

rows.grain: one row per fund, per year
rows.what_it_answers: Every stabilization fund's ending cash and ending market value, FY2011-FY2025, read off the trust tables in the annual reports.
rows.caution: ONLY PROVEN ROWS ARE HERE. Each exists because an identity the table states about itself closed -- beginning plus activity equals ending cash, ending cash plus unrealised equals ending market. A fund-year that is absent was refused, not zero. FY2023 refuses on OCR alone: its page prints the arithmetic correctly and the scanner returns the figure block as two tokens.

rows.grain: one row per year, per document
rows.what_it_answers: Which years of the receivables table publish and which refuse, with the reason, the column order as printed, both grand totals, and the ROLL-FORWARD carry.
rows.caution: THE ONLY CHECK IN THIS ARCHIVE THAT TESTS A YEAR AGAINST A DIFFERENT BOOK. One year's closing balance must be the next year's opening. Every readable pair ties to the cent except FY2017 to FY2018, which is $13,300.00 apart in two printed grand totals. A refused year is our instrument failing, not the town declining to print: all twelve publish the table and all twelve print a total.

rows.grain: one row per refused year
rows.what_it_answers: The thirteen years of the receivables table that will not publish, and why each one refuses.
rows.caution: THE REASONS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE AND THAT IS THE USE OF THIS TABLE. Six were already proved by `receivables`. FY2016 and FY2019 are CROPPED -- BALANCES is off the right edge of the image -- so no re-scan or parser recovers them; only an uncropped copy from the Town does. Three more are torn by scan distortion exactly where the GRAND TOTAL row sits.

rows.grain: one row per refused page
rows.what_it_answers: The capital-plan pages that would not read, with the total the page states and its columns as printed.
rows.caution: A REFUSAL IS NOT A READING. These are kept out of `capital_plans` deliberately, because a row saying `refused` inside the data marked its own page as read and cleared it off the ingestion queue.

rows.grain: one row per municipality, per year
rows.what_it_answers: What every Massachusetts municipality spent on HEALTH INSURANCE, as the Division of Local Services reports it. All 351 towns and cities, so Lunenburg can be set beside anyone rather than only its usual eleven peers.
rows.caution: ALL 351 MUNICIPALITIES, NOT THE PEER SET. Filter by `dor_code` or `municipality` before aggregating or the figures are the Commonwealth’s, not a town’s. It is REPORTED SPENDING and not a rate, a plan design or a headcount — a town spending less may insure fewer people rather than insure them more cheaply, and nothing here distinguishes the two.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, expenditure FROM dls_health_insurance WHERE municipality LIKE 'Lunenburg%' ORDER BY fy

rows.grain: one row per municipality, per year
rows.what_it_answers: The same DLS series for SELF-INSURED municipalities, which report a fund rather than a premium: starting balance, revenues, expenditures and closing fund balance.
rows.caution: A SELF-INSURED TOWN AND AN INSURED ONE ARE NOT COMPARABLE LINE FOR LINE. This is a fund’s activity; `dls_health_insurance` is money paid out. Adding them together, or ranking towns across the two, compares a premium with a cash flow. The `flag` column is the Commonwealth’s own marking and must be read before use.

rows.grain: one row per co-op participant town or measure
rows.what_it_answers: The ski co-operative: which towns send athletes, how many, and what is paid — the one athletics programme Lunenburg runs jointly with other districts.
rows.caution: A CO-OP TOTAL IS NOT A ONE-TOWN TOTAL, which is the whole reason this is its own table. Its figures cover every participating town, so setting them beside another sport’s Lunenburg-only cost compares two different populations. `cell` carries the spreadsheet coordinate each figure was read from, per rule 13.

rows.grain: one row per CSV file this database was built from
rows.what_it_answers: Which files, by sha256, produced the figures in this database — so a reader can tell whether it still matches them. The database is a derived read model rebuilt from the CSVs; this is the only thing that records WHEN and FROM WHAT, which is what makes staleness detectable.
rows.caution: A hash here is of the bytes at build time. It says nothing about whether those bytes were correct, only whether they have since changed. Ask scripts/db_freshness.py rather than reading this by hand.
rows.default_query: SELECT count(*) AS files FROM build_inputs

rows.grain: one row per fact about this build (key, value)
rows.what_it_answers: When this database was built, and how many input files it hashed. It exists because a four-day-old copy of receivables.csv went on crediting ten annual-report pages as read after the rows were deleted for not proving, and nothing anywhere recorded the copy’s age.
rows.caution: built_at is when the build ran, not when the underlying documents were published. Values are stored as text.
rows.default_query: SELECT key, value FROM build_meta ORDER BY key

rows.grain: one row per account per report (8 reports: FY2023-FY2026 period 13, general fund and special funds)
rows.what_it_answers: The school department's own MUNIS year-to-date budget reports at the CLOSE of each fiscal year (period 13): original and revised budget, expended, encumbered and available, per account. Read from the published spreadsheets the Town delivered on 6 October 2026, tied to every total the sheet prints.
rows.caution: Fiscal year and period come from the FILENAME -- the workbooks state neither. Period 13 is the closed year; period 12 is June before the closing entries.

rows.grain: one row per account in fund 1300, FY2026 periods 1-13
rows.what_it_answers: The FY2026 trial balance of fund 1300 per account: beginning balance, debits, credits, net change, ending balance -- as the MUNIS report prints it.
rows.caution: Fund 1300 only. One fiscal year (FY2026); the workbook's own cell B5 states the year and is checked against the filename.

rows.grain: one row per journal line in fund 1300, FY2026
rows.what_it_answers: Every journal line behind the fund 1300 trial balance: period, journal, source, effective date, reference, debits, credits, running balance. What moved each fund 1300 account, line by line.
rows.caution: `is_soy_opening_balance` marks the start-of-year opening entry, which is a balance and not an activity -- exclude it when summing a year's movement.

rows.grain: one row per printed cell of a teacher salary schedule: district, schedule, step, lane
rows.what_it_answers: What each district's teachers' contract PRINTS as the pay scale, by step and lane, for Lunenburg and the districts it is compared with -- the question an average salary cannot answer, because an average also carries who is employed at which step. `read` says how each cell was read (text layer, OCR confirmed by a second reading, or by eye off the page) and `flag` names any cell that fails a check: rising along steps and across lanes, and equal to the previous year times the increase the contract states.
rows.caution: A SCALE, not pay: no headcount by step or lane is here, and longevity, stipends and degree add-ons paid outside the grid are not in it -- Lunenburg's own longevity adds to step 13. Lane names and step counts differ by district, so compare like lanes by name, never by position. `fy` repeats within a document where two schedules apply in one year; split on `schedule`. Several DESE filings are expired contracts: check `contract_period` and teacher_salary_schedule_docs before calling a figure current.
rows.default_query: SELECT district, step, lane, salary FROM teacher_salary_schedules WHERE fy = 2026 AND step = '1' ORDER BY district, lane

rows.grain: one row per teachers’ contract read for its salary schedules
rows.what_it_answers: Which contract each schedule came from: publisher, address, the publisher's filename, the contract period, what pdf_kind.py found the PDF to be, which fiscal years were read, and anything that could not be.
rows.caution: DESE publishes the latest contract a district SUBMITTED, which is often an expired one; `contract_period` is the test of whether a schedule is current.
rows.default_query: SELECT district, contract_period, fiscal_years_read, status FROM teacher_salary_schedule_docs

rows.grain: one row per journal line: every posting behind every school account, general fund AND every school special fund (grants, circuit breaker, revolving, school choice, lunch, gifts), FY2023 period 0 to FY2026 period 13
rows.what_it_answers: Who the schools paid, when, from which fund and account, and why the books moved: every invoice (API), payroll posting (PRJ), purchase order and its liquidation (POE/POL/POM), budget entry (BUC original, BUA transfer), year-end reclassification (GEN) and receipt (CRP). The all-funds view no budget document gives: a cost leaving the general fund for a grant shows as both halves. Our redacted reading of the Town's 1,744-page MUNIS journal report; the raw is private.
rows.caution: REDACTED under TJ's rule: recipients of school services (children, and families acting for them) are masked with every residue; providers and vendors are named. `vendor` = 'individual (redacted)' is a masked family payee, blank = the Town printed no payee; `name_basis` says why a person is shown. `posts_to` splits actual from encumbrance from budget -- sum only one. Payroll is dollars by account, not people. FY2026's year-end close is not posted in this run, so FY26 encumbrances are still open. Every line is NET (CLAUDE.md rule 11).

rows.grain: one row per school account (3,356), with the FY2026 figures the journal report prints

rows.caution: FY2026 figures only; earlier years are in munis_school_ytd (tied to this journal for all 939 accounts both hold). Includes org 13012 School Non-Recurring, which the period-13 spreadsheets lack.

rows.grain: one row per district per document that names it, per comparison set
rows.what_it_answers: WHICH DISTRICTS Lunenburg is compared with, and WHO CHOSE them. `official` is every district the district itself named as comparable in a budget document -- the Budget Task Force's list in the FY2026 proposed budget, the RADAR selection and DART columns in the FY2020 one -- one row per district per document, with the page and the words that name it. `project-six` is this project's own set, chosen with no recorded criterion.
rows.caution: Two sets, two choosers: never present `project-six` as the district's choice, or `official` as ours. A district appears once per document that names it, so count DISTINCT `dese_org_code`, not rows. `district_as_printed` is the document's spelling (Ayer-Shirley); join on `dese_org_code`. Checked by scripts/check_comparison_sets.py.
rows.default_query: SELECT set_id, chosen_by, district_as_printed, dese_org_code, fy_of_list, source_page FROM comparison_sets ORDER BY set_id, fy_of_list, district_as_printed

rows.grain: one row per district per school year (fy = the school year: 2025 is 2024-25)

rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1976 edition: school fuel oil consumed (gallons, barrels) and degree days, 1972-73 to 1974-75. No money.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`. Units are gallons, barrels and degree days, never dollars.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_energy_use ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per position change
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1977 edition: the School Committee's PROPOSED staff reductions and additions in the FY-78 request, with the dollar effect of each. A proposal, not an outcome.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`. PROPOSED stage: what the request planned, not what happened.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_school_staff_changes ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per fact
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1978 edition: the town facts page -- county, area, road miles, census population, assessed valuation and tax rate, one fact per row, as printed.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`. Mixed units, one per row: never summed.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_town_facts ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per jurisdiction
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1978 edition: per capita expenditure and property tax per capita, fiscal year 1976, for Lunenburg against the Massachusetts and fifty-state averages (U.S. Census Bureau data, as the report prints them).
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`. Per capita dollars, another publisher's figures as printed.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_per_capita_comparison ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per line
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1978 edition: income and expenses of the 250th Anniversary / Old Home Week committee.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_committee_income_expenses ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per measure
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1979 edition: the Treasurer's nineteen-line comparison of financial performance data, FY 1975 - FY 1979 (taxes committed and outstanding, debt, valuation, cash invested, free cash, temporary notes).
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`. Mixed units and ratios, one measure per row: never summed down a column.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_financial_performance ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per line
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1980 edition: analysis and comparison of surplus revenue and free cash, fiscal 1976-1980, and fiscal 1981 ESTIMATED.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year (`1981`), never `FY1981`. Split on `status`. The last column is an ESTIMATE, labelled in `column_meaning`; the others are actuals (rule 1).
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_surplus_free_cash ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per program (or month)
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1959-1970 editions: the Welfare Department's table -- persons aided (1962-1967) or average case load (1959), expended, reimbursements from the State, Federal government, cities and towns, and net cost to the Town, by program; 1967 also prints persons aided and expended in four months (family `welfare-case-load-months`).
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning` from the printed header. `edition` is the book's printed year, never `FY`. Split on `status` and on `table_family`: an average case load (1959) is not a count of persons aided. Calendar-year actuals; the money is the Welfare Board's, net of reimbursements, not the town's whole cost (rule 11).
rows.default_query: SELECT edition, label, v1, v2, v3, v4, column_meaning FROM report_welfare_aid ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per tax type in one levy year
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1961-1962 editions: the Tax Collector's report by levy year -- committed, collected, abated, abatement rescinded, refunded, added to tax title, balance -- and betterments. The other 1959-1970 editions print the same table and land in `tax_collection`, which has no column for `Abatement Rescinded`; these two stay here so that figure is not dropped.
rows.caution: v1..v8 are ORDINALS named in `column_meaning`; v1 is the levy YEAR, not money. Split on `status` and `table_family`. Actuals.
rows.default_query: SELECT edition, label, v1, v2, v3, v4, v5, column_meaning FROM report_tax_collection_by_levy_year ORDER BY edition, page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per cost component
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1959 edition: the costs the School Building Assistance Commission APPROVED for the Jr.-Sr. High School (general contract, architect, equipment, site), on which the State reimbursed a share.
rows.caution: An APPROVED cost base, not a payment and not a debt figure: never summed with `report_debt` or with spending. Split on `status`.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, column_meaning FROM report_school_building_approved_costs ORDER BY page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per cost line
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1961 edition: the School Building Addition Committee's cost of the new wing, work on the existing building and committee expense, to completion.
rows.caution: A project's cost to completion, not a year's spending and not the 2001-2010 capital-projects fund schedule. Split on `status`.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, column_meaning FROM report_capital_project_costs ORDER BY page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: NEW with the 1967 edition: the registration and distribution of minors -- boys and girls by age band, and where they were enrolled.
rows.caution: COUNTS of children, never dollars. One edition. Split on `status`.
rows.default_query: SELECT label, v1, v2, v3, column_meaning FROM report_school_census_minors ORDER BY page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per department per annual report
rows.what_it_answers: The town's OWN contents page of each annual report, FY2011-FY2025: every department and body it lists, the PRINTED page range of its report and the PDF pages that range lands on, or the town's own words `No Report Submitted`.
rows.caution: printed_from/printed_to are the page numbers the book prints at its feet; pdf_from/pdf_to are positions in the PDF. A body absent from the contents page is NOT the same as `no report submitted`.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, department, pdf_from, pdf_to, state FROM report_index WHERE state = 'no report submitted' ORDER BY fy, department

rows.grain: one row per signature on a department report
rows.what_it_answers: Who signed each department's report in the FY2013-FY2025 annual reports, with the title they printed beside their name, attributed to the department by the town's own contents page.
rows.caution: Machine-read from OCR: names and titles carry OCR errors and a few rows are misattributed. A signature is who signed that year's report, not a term of office.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, department, person, title, page FROM report_signatures ORDER BY fy, department

rows.grain: one row per body
rows.what_it_answers: Per body, which years it filed an annual report, which years the contents page printed `No Report Submitted`, and which years it was not listed at all. DERIVED from report_index; no edition column.
rows.caution: Three states, not two: `said none` is the town recording that a body sent nothing; a year in neither list means the body was not on the contents page. Filing is a convention, not a statutory duty.
rows.default_query: SELECT body, filed, said_none, of_years, first_filed, last_filed FROM report_filing ORDER BY filed DESC

rows.grain: one row per printed line
rows.what_it_answers: Page 60 of the FY2011 appropriations schedule, the page the generic extract first missed, read separately: one row per printed line with its program and the five money columns, published only where a program's lines sum to the subtotal printed beneath them.
rows.caution: Values are TEXT as printed; cast to compare. report_appropriations now also holds this page (as check failed), so do not add the two together.
rows.default_query: SELECT program, label, appropriated_or_forward, total_expended FROM report_appropriations_supplement ORDER BY page, line_no

rows.grain: one row per account per report year
rows.what_it_answers: What the town HELD on 30 June, by bank and fund, as the Treasurer's Cash listing in each annual report prints it, 1960-2025. The listing that names the general (Bartholomew) Stabilization Fund.
rows.caution: `column` = 'prior year' rows are the previous year reprinted for comparison; filter to 'as printed' or each year counts twice. A cash balance, not an appropriation.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, held_as, amount, page FROM treasurers_cash WHERE "column" = 'as printed' ORDER BY fy DESC, held_as

rows.grain: one row per debt issue per due year per report
rows.what_it_answers: The debt repayment schedule PER ISSUE: principal, interest and fee due each future year, from the reports' text layer (FY2011-FY2025 where the page has one).
rows.caution: Every report reprints the whole schedule, so a due year appears once per report; split on report_fy. Read `column_foots`: many tables are off by a dollar of rounding, some do not foot at all, and image-only years are in debt_repayment_detail_refused instead.
rows.default_query: SELECT report_fy, issue, due_fy, principal, interest, total, column_foots FROM debt_repayment_detail WHERE report_fy = (SELECT MAX(report_fy) FROM debt_repayment_detail) ORDER BY issue_seq, due_fy

rows.grain: one row per grade per step per schedule year
rows.what_it_answers: The town salary schedule printed in the annual report, hourly rate by grade and step, as printed in four reports (schedule years from the FY2010, FY2015, FY2016 and FY2022 books).
rows.caution: A schedule the report prints, tied to a town meeting article; not the teachers' contract. `basis` says how each rate was read (text layer, OCR, Textract); `confirmed_by` names the second printing that agrees where one exists.
rows.default_query: SELECT schedule_fy, grade, step, rate, basis FROM salary_schedule ORDER BY schedule_fy, CAST(grade AS INTEGER), CAST(step AS INTEGER)

rows.grain: one row per fund per measure
rows.what_it_answers: The FY2025 TRUST FUNDS summary matrix: 29 funds, their group subtotals and grand total, across 14 measures (beginning principal and earnings, income, gains, transfers, ending cash, ending market value).
rows.caution: One report year only. `kind` separates fund rows from 'group subtotal' and 'grand total'; sum only kind = 'fund' or totals are counted twice.
rows.default_query: SELECT "column" AS fund, measure, amount FROM trust_fund_matrix WHERE kind = 'fund' AND measure LIKE 'ending%' ORDER BY fund

rows.grain: one row per trust account per year
rows.what_it_answers: The TRUST FUND BALANCE DETAIL list: every trust and stabilization fund by account number with its balance, FY2024-FY2025 (account 8124 is the general Stabilization Fund).
rows.caution: A balance list with nothing printed to add up, so rows are unchecked by arithmetic; `ledger_agrees` records a cross-check against the ledger where one was made.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, account, name, balance FROM trust_fund_balances ORDER BY fy DESC, account

rows.grain: one row per contractor name per year
rows.what_it_answers: Contractors printed inside the 1959-2010 school rosters -- mostly school bus contractors -- kept apart from staff so they are not counted as employees.
rows.caution: Names, not contracts: no amounts, no terms. Only years whose roster printed a contractors block.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, name, role_raw, page FROM staff_roster_contractors ORDER BY fy, name

rows.grain: one row per project per option per program year
rows.what_it_answers: The two (or more) CAPITAL PROGRAM OPTIONS the town meeting was asked to choose between, priced to the same total, with the CPC ranking and cost of each project.
rows.caution: Options, not what was bought: the vote that chose between them is in the town meeting record. `kind` separates projects from printed totals.
rows.default_query: SELECT program_fy, option, cpc_ranking, department, project, project_cost FROM capital_program_options WHERE kind = 'project' ORDER BY program_fy, option, CAST(cpc_ranking AS INTEGER)

rows.grain: one row per expense category per year
rows.what_it_answers: Monty Tech (Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical) district expenses by category, read off the chart in the FY2025 annual town report.
rows.caution: THE REGIONAL VOCATIONAL DISTRICT'S spending, NOT the Lunenburg school district's and not Lunenburg's assessment. Read by OCR from a chart image; `kind` separates the total from its categories.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, category, amount FROM monty_tech_expenses WHERE kind <> 'total' ORDER BY fy, category

rows.grain: one row per figure per fund per page read
rows.what_it_answers: Every figure on report pages READ by eye (not OCR), FY2011 onward -- special revenue schedules, trust listings, valuation -- each re-proved against the total the page itself prints.
rows.caution: Long format: one row per cell (`column`, `value`), so pivot before comparing funds. `status` = 'no check' where the page prints no total. A balance or flow per fund as printed; which dataset a page feeds is in its proof.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, page, fund_name, "column", value, status FROM pages_read ORDER BY fy, page, fund_number LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per transfer into or out of a stabilization fund
rows.what_it_answers: Money moved INTO or OUT OF the stabilization funds, quoted from the town meeting articles the annual reports print, with the clause that moves it.
rows.caution: Twelve rows, not a complete ledger: only transfers found in printed article text. Read `confidence` -- two are possible duplicates and one may be a misread deposit.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, fund, direction, amount, confidence, quote FROM stabilization_flows ORDER BY fy

rows.grain: one row per name per position per edition
rows.what_it_answers: TOWN officials and staff, every edition 1959-2010 and FY2011-FY2025: the officers' directory and department rosters, who was elected or appointed to what, with term where printed.
rows.caution: Names as printed: spelling and initials vary between editions, so a person is not a stable key. A listing is not a term of service or a paid post; no salary, no FTE. School staff are in staff_roster_entries.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, section, position, name, term, page FROM town_roster_entries ORDER BY year DESC, section, position LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per fiscal year, per printed table, per edition
rows.what_it_answers: New growth (added valuation, the prior-year rate, the revenue it added, new structures where printed), total assessed valuation and the tax rate, before FY2011, read from the annual town reports with edition and line number.
rows.caution: ONE ROW PER PRINTING: a year reprinted in several editions appears several times, so pick one `edition` or group by `fy` before summing. Split on `status`: `check failed` rows are the town's own arithmetic not closing (the FY2008-FY2009 editions print the current year's rate in the prior-rate column; FY2009 prints an added valuation the state does not). Disagreements between editions and with the DLS files are in `cross_edition` and `cross_state`.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, edition, ng_added_valuation, ng_rate, ng_revenue, status FROM report_new_growth_history WHERE printed_table = 'new_growth' ORDER BY fy, edition LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per name per wage-list page per report year
rows.what_it_answers: What the Town paid each person, by name, in the Town & School Employee Gross Wages list each annual report prints, FY2011-FY2025: the amount, and the department where FY2011-FY2017 print one.
rows.caution: GROSS pay in the CALENDAR year the list prints, every fund: overtime, details and stipends included; not salary, not FTE, not what a post costs with benefits. Names as printed, so a person is not a stable key across years. `status` says whether every money figure on the page was captured; `reconciliation` names the instrument (text layer or Textract).
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, COUNT(*) AS names, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) AS paid FROM gross_wages GROUP BY fy ORDER BY fy

rows.grain: one row per warrant article per Town Meeting
rows.what_it_answers: Each Town Meeting article FY2011-FY2025, as the annual report's minutes print it: the subject, the result, the amount where one is printed, and the Finance Committee and Select Board recommendations.
rows.caution: `amount_as_printed` is the text the minutes print, not a parsed figure. A vote to appropriate is not what was spent.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, meeting, COUNT(*) AS articles FROM town_meeting_votes GROUP BY fy, meeting ORDER BY fy

rows.grain: one row per scholarship or prize fund per account per fiscal year
rows.what_it_answers: Each school scholarship and prize fund held by the Town, FY2011-FY2025: balances, earnings and paid_out, the money that left the fund net of what came in.
rows.caution: paid_out is money leaving a fund; that it was awards is our reading. account = 'stock' rows are share holdings of two prizes and pay nothing out. A fund missing from a year has no proven row that year, which is about our reading, not the town.
rows.default_query: SELECT fy, fund, paid_out, net_earnings, ending_cash FROM scholarship_funds WHERE account = 'fund' ORDER BY fund, fy

rows.grain: one row per fund whose purpose a record states
rows.what_it_answers: What each school scholarship is for, quoted exactly from the document that states it, with its page.
rows.caution: kind = 'transcript' is machine captions of a meeting recording: a finding aid, not a record. A fund with no row has no stated purpose in what was searched.
rows.default_query: SELECT fund, purpose, kind, year, document, page FROM scholarship_purposes ORDER BY fund

rows.grain: one row per category the Fire Department printed for a year, plus a total row where a total is printed
rows.what_it_answers: How many calls the Fire Department reported each year, 1959-FY2025, and in what categories, read from every annual report.
rows.caution: Split on `row_role` before summing: `total` rows and `part` rows are the same calls counted twice. `group_ties` says whether a year's parts reach its printed total, and some years do not; nothing was adjusted. Categories change by era, inspections are inside some totals and outside others, and `our_grouping` is our judgement rather than anything printed. A count of calls is not a count of emergencies, and no year here says why the number moved.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, value FROM series_fire_calls WHERE row_group='calls' AND row_role='total' ORDER BY year

rows.grain: one row per series family per annual report edition
rows.what_it_answers: Which annual report editions were checked for each year-by-year series, and whether the series is printed there.
rows.caution: A family with no row for an edition was not looked at. `not printed` names the pages looked at, and is a statement about those pages.

rows.grain: one row per programme season (calendar year)
rows.what_it_answers: How many residents took part in the senior property tax work-off programme each season, the hours and the dollars abated, with the source of each figure.
rows.caution: Each figure has its own citation, quote and qualifier; a value may be approximate or come from a board minute rather than the annual report. Read the `_qualifier` and `_kind` columns before comparing years.

rows.grain: one row per printed figure on a Tax Collector's levy-year table, per annual report edition
rows.what_it_answers: What the Tax Collector's tables print by levy year for the annual report editions the other collection datasets do not hold.
rows.caution: Only the editions missing elsewhere: `series_coverage` says which. Split on `row_role` before summing. Figures are as printed, not reconciled to the ledger. Rows noted `misread` were read off the page image and are backed by their column's printed total.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_tax_collection_holes ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed figure on a Monty Tech budget, assessment or Educational Plan table
rows.what_it_answers: What the Monty Tech reports print about the district's budget, member-town assessments, enrolment and grants, by year.
rows.caution: FY2017 pp140-149 carry most of the rows; other editions hold Educational Plan totals. Lunenburg's own Monty Tech appropriation is `held elsewhere` (report_appropriations). Many groups miss their printed total by a few dollars, consistent with whole-dollar display, and `group_ties` labels each. A budget figure is not spending. Figures printed in parentheses are negative here.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_monty_tech_budgets ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per item or printed total in a capital plan, per edition
rows.what_it_answers: What the capital plan listed, item by item, for the editions capital_plans does not hold.
rows.caution: An item listed is an item presented or planned, not one funded or bought. Split on `row_role`. FY2023's table prints fewer items than its own text counts, and FY2025 holds both options for FY26 (one was voted): read `note`.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_capital_plan_holes ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per revolving fund per town meeting vote
rows.what_it_answers: What spending limit town meeting voted for each revolving fund, year by year.
rows.caution: These are voted LIMITS, not spending or balances. `year_basis` says what `year` means: mostly the town meeting year, not always the fiscal year the limit applies to. Passed-over articles are left out, and where a vote amended the warrant the voted figure is used.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_revolving_fund_limits ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed fact (population, voters, road miles, area) per edition
rows.what_it_answers: What the reports print for population, registered voters, road miles and area over time.
rows.caution: Federal, state and town census populations are kept apart by source and are not one series: never difference across sources. A date of printing is not a date of counting, and later editions repeat old figures; read `year_basis`.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_town_facts ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per ballot question per precinct per yes, no or blank count
rows.what_it_answers: How each local ballot question went, by precinct, 1960-FY2025.
rows.caution: Split on `row_role` before summing. A few precinct columns do not reach the printed total and are kept as printed: `group_ties` labels them. FY2012, FY2014, FY2016 and FY2024 are held in ballot_questions. Includes liquor licence and similar questions, not only money.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_ballot_questions_local ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per grant, printed total, or account line
rows.what_it_answers: Which applicants and projects the Cultural Council funded, and what total each year's report prints.
rows.caution: Lists exist for only some years; other years print totals or program counts only (`series_coverage`). A grant awarded is not a grant spent. Revenue and account-form rows share this table: split on `row_group`.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_cultural_council_grants ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed count of a service, nursing visit or disease case for Lunenburg
rows.what_it_answers: What Nashoba reported doing for Lunenburg each year: inspections, tests, nursing visits, communicable disease cases.
rows.caution: Categories change by era and are not one series without checking. 2001-2007 are held in report_dept_activity. Some editions repeat a prior year's figures. Small disease counts are reported counts, and a count that moved does not say why. The Town's own nurses are not here.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_nashoba_public_health ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed count of calls, incidents, arrests, complaints, stops, accidents or custody
rows.what_it_answers: What the Police Department reports it handled each year.
rows.caution: The headline's wording moves from miscellaneous calls to incidents to calls for service and is kept as printed, so a jump can be a change of definition. Editions contradict each other about prior years: each figure is as printed in its own edition. A count of calls is not a count of crimes.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_police_activity ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed test figure for a school, grade, subject, level and year
rows.what_it_answers: What the annual reports print of MCAS results, against the state where printed.
rows.caution: The scale changes: Advanced/Proficient to 2016, Meeting/Exceeding from 2017 (`our_grouping`). Scales are not comparable across that change. Number and percent of the same level are separate rows: split on `unit`. Some tables head a different year from their edition; those are noted. A school's reported share is not a measure of teaching.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_mcas_from_reports ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed count, share or state indicator figure
rows.what_it_answers: How many students the reports say received special education, against the state, and each state indicator printed.
rows.caution: Reported shares and rates, not counts of children, unless `unit` says students. Suppressed figures have a blank `value` and a note. FY2013 prints two denominators. Some scores are scaled scores, not index scores: read `unit`. An indicator figure does not say what caused it.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_sped_indicators ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per figure on a one-off finance table
rows.what_it_answers: Single-year finance tables with no series of their own: 1962 tax rate recap, 1981 assessment example, FY2019 revenue and changes, FY2024 fund balance roll-forward, FY2025 enrolment and Chapter 70.
rows.caution: Not a series. Years cannot be compared across tables; filter on `edition` and `row_group`.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_oneoff_finance ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed count of meals, rides or clients
rows.what_it_answers: How many Meals on Wheels meals and senior van rides the Council on Aging reports.
rows.caution: Not like for like: some years print averages per day or month, some approximate, and some meal counts include supper and weekend meals (`note`, `unit`). Editions disagree on prior years. FY2011-14 and FY2020-25 print no counts.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_coa_services ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed figure for circulation, visits, borrowers, volumes or hours
rows.what_it_answers: How much the library's reports say it was used each year.
rows.caution: Split on `row_role`. Material categories change by era, and a change in what circulates (digital items) changes the total's meaning. Editions disagree on prior years. Two years' parts do not reach their printed total: `group_ties`.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_library_usage ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed count of people aided or dollars paid
rows.what_it_answers: How many veterans and families were aided and what was paid and reimbursed, in the years the reports print it.
rows.caution: Most editions print nothing: `series_coverage` says which. Dollars paid and dollars reimbursed are different quantities. FY2022 and FY2023 print per-month averages that may be annual figures divided by 12; kept as printed. FY2021 p79 also prints West Boylston, which is not here.

rows.what_it_answers: Catch-all: small one-offs. Attendance Officer calls, trips, miles and contacts by month 1959-1979; the list of buildings the DPW maintains 2008-FY2013; retirees thanked at Annual Town Meeting 2002-FY2012; easement and land-right articles (1992, 1997); the FY2017 forest stewardship plan grants; the 1963 school lunch summary box; the FY2019 public access cable expense shares.
rows.caution: Split on `row_role` before summing; `group_ties` says whether printed parts reach a printed total, and nothing was adjusted to make one. A row with a blank `value` is printed text, held in `quote`. `misread` in `note` means the figure was read from the page image because the text layer garbles it. Unrelated one-offs: filter on `row_group` before reading anything across rows.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_small_one_offs ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200

rows.grain: one row per printed figure, name or text item, per edition, as the page prints it
rows.what_it_answers: Monty Tech lists and sports notes. Lists and counts from the Montachusett Regional Vocational Technical School district report: trades and programs offered (1967, 1969, 1988, 2001), the community projects each trade listed 2002-2009, athletic team records (wins, losses, ties; league records as printed) and team counts 2001-FY2019, and MCAS passing rates, proficient/advanced shares, results tables and graduation competency percentages 2001-FY2025, all as printed. The FY2011-FY2025 prose shop reports are entered one paragraph per shop (text as the page layer reads it) with each shop's enrollment and every figure in the prose, and the FY2012-FY2014 student group accountability tables (performance and progress by group). Names of outstanding athletes and of students recognised in the press are not entered.
rows.caution: Split on `row_role` before summing; `group_ties` says whether printed parts reach a printed total, and nothing was adjusted to make one. A row with a blank `value` is printed text, held in `quote`. `misread` in `note` means the figure was read from the page image because the text layer garbles it. Paragraph quotes follow the text layer and keep its OCR errors; not every prose figure was re-read against the page image. Team records count games, not money.
rows.default_query: SELECT year, edition, row_group, measure, value, unit, row_role FROM series_monty_tech_lists ORDER BY year, row_group LIMIT 200
